column1: # DevCouncil `--json` invocations whose stdout must hold exactly one JSON object.
# Fields are TAB-separated. The first is the mode; the rest are argv, passed to
# the process directly — there is no shell here, so nothing needs quoting.
# `{PY}` is replaced with the interpreter the harness resolved and `{ROOT}` with
# the throwaway project it initialised, so every entry runs against a real,
# freshly-scaffolded repository rather than the developer's own checkout.
# Every entry here reproduced a failure against the pre-fix CLI, except where a
# comment says otherwise. Both outcomes are covered on purpose: a command that
# succeeds and a command that rejects its arguments owe stdout the same one
# object, and it was the rejecting paths that were emitting zero.
# --- dev cost: the confirmed leak, both shapes ---------------------------------
# --- dev report: five branches that did their work and returned ----------------
# --- dev go: the orchestrator, whose whole console output was narration --------
# The second reaches plan.py, which was writing a provider error onto stdout
# ahead of the payload; the first is rejected before planning starts.
# --- dev boot: the whole setup phase used to run onto the payload stream --------
# `{ROOT}` is already initialised by the harness, so this exercises boot's
# re-init path plus the doctor table, both of which were writing to stdout.
# --skip-api-key keeps it non-interactive; boot would force that anyway off a TTY.
# --- streaming commands, whose progress ran around the payload -----------------
# `--jsonl` is the sibling contract: stdout is a newline-delimited JSON stream,
# and the cursor line was the last, unparseable thing a consumer read.
# --- commands that already honoured the contract, kept as the control ----------
# If these ever fail, the harness itself is wrong rather than the CLI.
